The cases of two separate tactical lasers have seemingly been pulled apart and put back together again.
A capacitive circuit from a pulse laser and the controls from a Talon interceptor flight computer have turned these two previously innocuous light defense lasers in to a deadly spitting cobra. Relatively short range and energy hungry, but deadly in a brawl.

What appears at first sight to be a normal point defense laser, the laser delivery chamber has been heavily modified.
Several rotating refractive industrial emeralds have been mounted inside a gas-filled magnetic containment field.
Upon operation, a salvo of plasma and high energy laser pulses leave this chamber in approximately the direction of the chosen target.
A high frequency excimer laser, used by the Junk Pirates to etch travel directions, shopping lists and floral patterns on to layabout space debris.

Hot shrapnel is released from a guided canister at high speeds, designed to give a warm welcome to overzealous fighter fleets.
The cannon fires a pair of canisters at once before reloading.

Hot shrapnel is released from a guided canister at high speeds, designed to give a warm welcome to overzealous fighter fleets.
The launcher fires a single canister at once before reloading.

Hot shrapnel is released from a guided canister at high speeds, designed to give a warm welcome to overzealous fighter fleets.
This small mount carries a single guided canister – which is reloaded slowly over time.

The only difference between this and a typical dumb-fire gas-release escape pod is the substitution of real people for several carefully sculpted highly volatile lifesize statues, made out of suitably explosive chemical pastes and compounds.
Competitions are regularly held at Karkov Academy, and those individuals who produce the most aesthetically pleasing figures are held in high regard indeed.

The devastating right hook of the Junk Pirates' Tangerine.
This weapon fires a modified thermal pulse, causing high damage and scrambling systems.
This built in weapon is capable of significant initial burst damage making it a highly potent strike weapon on the swift and mobile frigate. The reactors on the Tangerine recharge the Haymaker relatively slowly, so the weapon loses utility in extended battles against superior sustained firepower.

The devastating right hook of the Junk Pirates' Tangerine, this version is that fitted to the Blue Tangerine, having a higher energy payload but reduced firing frequency.
This weapon fires a modified thermal pulse, causing high damage and scrambling systems.
This built in weapon is capable of significant initial burst damage making it a highly potent strike weapon on the swift and mobile frigate. The reactors on the Tangerine recharge the Haymaker relatively slowly, so the weapon loses utility in extended battles against superior sustained firepower.

The sting in the tail of the Junk Pirates' Langoustine.
Based on the Haymaker of the Tangerine, this weapon has a reduced damage but a much increased rate of fire.

The Stygian Drill is an immensely powerful industrial particle beam integrated directly into The Reaper. Continuous fire superheats the focused red-to-orange lance, scaling damage from 1,000 to 1,800 Fragmentation DPS over 3 seconds and tearing armor plating cleanly off target hulls.

The PICA – Particle Inverter / Charge Amplifier – claims to use a hitherto unknown (and subsequently unproven) process to weaponise the generous flux chambers of the Magpie.
By sinusoidally varying the charge ratings of particles held in the pre-firing chamber from plus 2 to negative 2 times base values, this generates a soup of plasma and antimatter which react to angrily discharge from the metalo-ceramic barrel via the reflective and resonant 'bassoon'. Huge positive and negative recoil cancel each other out in totality, and so the frame of the weapon can shift focus and maintain accuracy frighteningly well.
(at least, that's what it says in the user manual).
Whatever the truth of the physical processes – the weapon delivers an impressive volley of quickly moving and powerful energy charges in a straight line towards would-be aggressors, but the esoteric technology and large ordnance footprint make it fundamentally impractical for incorporation as a standalone weapon outside the frame of the Magpie.

A long-ranged energy support weapon, firing an unstable stream of ionized particles with the notable side effect of converting whatever it strikes into a 'lightning rod' for nearby electrostatically charged debris. Relatively undemanding in terms of engineering and support profile, though its efficacy leaves something to be desired.
A junk-built knockoff of the sector-standard Bhilai Exospace Ion Beam, the Electrostatic Shock Beam is claimed by Junk Pirate oral history to be reverse-engineered from a prototype stolen - usually, by incredible coincidence, by whoever happens to be telling the story - from the Chernobog Proving Grounds. The veracity of this information is somewhat in doubt, not least due to the claimed date of this event being significantly before the Collapse.

A robust and inexpensive autocannon with generous engineering specifications, easily mounted even to light vessels or those lacking in flux infrastructure. Nonstandard 'scrap' rounds produce unpredictable, though generally disappointing, effect on target.
The GA-X Industries Mk. I 'Scrapper' Autocannon, long out of production even before the Collapse, was once widely boasted to be capable of firing anything that would fit into the breech. Of course, when the blueprint was rediscovered in a remote Domain derelict outpost by Junk Pirate scavengers along with a filing cabinet full of incredibly preserved period advertising material, they took this as a challenge. Now back in steady use after uncounted centuries, the Junk Pirate 'standard' loadings for the Scrapper consist of grapeshot, heavy packing grease, non-Newtonian fluids, stale pizza crusts, stolen silverware, and everything in between.

A piece of standard industrial equipment turned starship armament, the affectionately christened 'Scrap Nailer' has been retooled to fire meter-long jagged spikes cut from scrap steel, damaged armour plating, or really just about any conductive metal that happens to be laying about.

More of a broad identification category than a discrete 'class' of weapons, the only traits universally shared by 'Scrapjet' missiles are their powerful engines, mid-weight payloads, and frankly deficient targeting systems. This particular weapon mount consists of four Scrapjets crudely affixed to a jury-rigged missile rack by a series of suspiciously oversized explosive bolts.

More of a broad identification category than a discrete 'class' of weapons, the only traits universally shared by 'Scrapjet' missiles are their powerful engines, mid-weight payloads, and frankly deficient targeting systems. This particular weapon mount consists of a standard double-arm missile rack fed by internal magazines which are routinely loaded far beyond their stated maximum capacity.

The Micro Scrapjet MLRS system fires a smaller version of her big sister the Scrapjet in the Micro Scrapjet. Similar behaviour is to be expected; with the various warhead types and including no particular guarantees that adjacent barn doors will be hit.
This MLRS fires micro scrapjets in extended ‘lucky dip’ salvoes of 8 and can be found on the right arm of the Orca pleasure craft.

A specialized dispenser that expels clouds of electrostatically charged chaff particles. When primed in proximity to hostile targets or incoming missiles, the particles release localized EMP arcs to disrupt guidance arrays and scrambled weapon sensors.
A heavy-duty light autocannon built directly into the frame of the Pitbull destroyer with enhanced cooling jackets, an accelerated feeder mechanism, and an aggressive cyclic rate.

A compact, lightened variant of the P.A.C.K. Ripsaw autocannon fitted onto the sponsons of Alyosha-class gunships. Delivers rapid bursts of kinetic flechettes designed to strip enemy shields during gunship attack runs.

Electromagnetically ejected from turreted rails on the paired sponsons of the Mitya-class heavy bomber. Its concentrated plasma-fusion warhead can breach the heaviest capital armor upon direct impact.

A specialized turreted point-defense pulse laser mounted on P.A.C.K. combat hulls. Emits high-intensity coherent bursts capable of rapidly incinerating incoming ordnance, while its magnetic-induction pulse scrambles missile guidance fins and engine nozzles, causing intercepted missiles to flame out and tumble off trajectory.
A compact rotary launcher mounted on P.A.C.K. gunships that ripples miniature self-guided Swarmer rockets to disperse enemy interceptors and intercept incoming light ordnance.
A customized light assault gun mounted on P.A.C.K. heavy gunships, firing rapid high-explosive shells to crack armor plating once target shields have been collapsed.
A miniaturized high-cyclic rotary point-defense cannon built for P.A.C.K. light attack craft, tearing through close-range missiles and drone swarms with dense ballistic spreads.

Anchored directly to the hull of the Copperhead-class freighter variant; rapid tracking and elevation are driven by an advanced super-cooled electromagnetic gimbal slaved to a high-spec targeting core. Punishing to shields at close range with best-in-class tracking speeds.

A fast frigate designed for getting in and out of trouble quickly, delivering some decent firepower with the medium energy turret mounted high above the bridge.
Decent flux reserves complement the main weapon and the omnidirectional shield, but it is relatively light and difficult to control, so can stand up poorly in a dogfight against a more nimble ship.

A mobile heavy ordnance platform. Slow for a small frigate, but highly manoeuvrable.
Due to its simple construction it is cheap yet reasonably robust, with front facing shields further improving its survivability.
Dangerous when encountered as part of a group due to its potentially lethal payload, but otherwise not particularly extraordinary.

The battle ready command platform for the Junk Pirate nobility.
With a high capacity for fuel and energy reserves supplementing the large omnidirectional shield and generous armour plating, the ship is deceptively tough to kill.
If the captain can swing this ship round in time to deliver his devastating ballistics-heavy broadside onto your direction, you need to think carefully about whether you want to stick around to watch the fireworks. Four missile hardpoints to the rear allow the ship to operate as a fire support platform.

A civilian freighter used by the Junk Pirates to transport goods, materials and people throughout the sector.
Whilst the ship itself is technically incapable of mounting shields; it carries a separate independent shield module for protection. One wing of the craft is complete with a fully functional, combat ready flight deck.
Hardy, fast and heavy hitting. A shortage of a shield makes it easier to kill than it looks, but it's cheap to produce, and not to be underestimated in the depths of a melee.

A light cruiser with a heavy hitting left hook, lightweight right jab and a decent enough jaw.
Similar in design, but different in tactical profile to the Dugong, delivered by engineers through a marginally successful programme trying to manufacture a cheaper, easier to field version.
The VIE plug-jets installed in this vessel make it hit quicker, but not as hard as the ammo-feeder equipped Dugong.

A front loaded energy-based Artillery platform, capable of bringing the main armament of two large energy weapons quickly to bear with her manoeuvring jets.
When infamous tinkerer Cerys Clattenberg presented this Cruiser to the King and declared it The Clattenberg Catapult, most people ignored both the creators chosen moniker and her subsequent execution. Dangerous as an artillery piece, but an expensive toy that needs constant protection from flanking when under duress.

Plan A: Win, Plan B: Escape, Plan C: Die, Plan D: Cleat.
Used to be regarded as a vital part of the safety protocols on Junk Pirates' ships - and for years the King felt comfortable in the knowledge that thousands of his loyal subjects would be living full and happy lives after escaping via the pods contained on the Cleat, which would be launched simply from the cargo bays of a defeated vessel - point towards the safest planetary body and launch the escape pod in to the gravity well where on board systems would allow the occupant to be delivered safely to the surface.
Unfortunately the systems were found wanting, and fatally decelerated bodies still appear to this day around the sector inside found pods.
The Cleat and the escape pod system have been happily repurposed in to an effective bomber by the ever resourceful Junk Pirate engineers.

The Boxer is characterised by thick armour plates around an inefficient but effective engine and controls system.
A powerful, fixed shield and some capable ballistic weaponry looking straight forward means it is a ship that you don't want to get caught in front of, but its sheer weight makes it unwieldy and slow.
Three mixed missile hardpoints and an additional ballistic turret with good coverage make the boxer capable of diverse roles.

An unholy fusion of the best parts of two Boxer class destroyers cut and welded together to create this hulk of a superdestroyer.
Controls and flux systems have been upgraded heavily, and this ship now relies largely on energy weaponry.

A defensive heavy frigate blessed with a useful, full coverage efficient shield system and some reasonable armour.
All this high technology has added cost and placed an unfortunate limit on the offensive capabilities of the craft, with the main capabilities coming from its missile payload.
Created in response to protestations from the Kingdom that all the other frigates are too exposed - leading to too many premature deaths. The King is looking forward to the time when the same people are complaining about this frigates lack of teeth.
Highly versatile and inexplicably symmetrical attack destroyer. Plug jets give great mobility, and the weapon loadout allows both good coverage and focus.
The darling of the Junk Pirate fleet, a versatile frigate with a medium energy turret and good mobility, augmented by Plug jets.

A flexible and robust support frigate. Relatively low mobility, but can bring great support with a medium ballistic mount and an acceptable shield system.
Fitted with a flare system providing good rear coverage, brave captains can forego point defense weaponry and hope for the best.

A ship fitted with great armour, great flux-handling, good mobility and an advanced drive field which allows the ship to increase in mobility with increased hard flux levels. It also has a built-in best-in-class strike weapon (the Haymaker energy blaster).
Almost the perfect hunter-killer frigate until you read the small print on the back page of the brochure and realise that the ship is guaranteed to enter a catastrophic overload when the Metastable Drive field is pushed too far. If you are lucky; this event will buy you enough time to turn the engines back on.

An experimental version of an experimental ship. The original Tangerine is fitted with great armour, great flux-handling, good mobility and an advanced drive field which allows the ship to increase in mobility with increased hard flux levels. It also has a built-in best-in-class strike weapon (the Haymaker energy blaster).
But it is guaranteed to enter a catastrophic overload when the Metastable Drive field is pushed too far. This ‘blue’ version is as piloted by the Circumstances, a brother and sister pair of outlaws, and appears to be tricked out with some fairly kooky time-bending tech layered on top of the already frightening loadout of the Tangerine.

Heavily armed, slow and modestly armoured carrier with an advanced shield and systems, the Orca represents (to some) the pinnacle of the Junk Pirates' bizarre breed of technology.
Versatile ballistic and energy mounts all around the perimeter of the craft allow for effective assault or defensive variants. It is unwise to engage this craft in a frontal assault, but if outnumbered or flanked by surprise, the relatively weak rear can be taken advantage of.

The preferred escort fighter for the Junk Pirates' fleet, produced largely within the region of Backspin, the second planet of the Breh'Inni system.
This is the spiritual home of the fighter pilots of the Junk Pirates' fleet, and as such the planet's orbit is thick with scarred, spinning hulls of the staple death-bucket, the Spike. Most of these are as a result of the training exercises, but some are returned hulls brought back by sentimental types.
For the fighter pilots lucky, or skilful enough, to show a degree of survivability in this oft-maligned entry model, they will be promoted to a far more expensive, but less easily aerated craft, the Shard.
More armour and better armaments in a slightly bulkier frame means more hot dinners at the post-sortie ho-down, and more business for opposition funeral directors.

A light freighter, ostensibly a couple of small engines attached to a frame, with the means to carry any of a number of cargo canisters or crates.
Very weak offensively and defensively, but it suits the Junk Pirates for inter-system logistics.
This model carries a small energy turret.

A light freighter, ostensibly a couple of small engines attached to a frame, with the means to carry any of a number of cargo canisters or crates.
Very weak offensively and defensively, but it suits the Junk Pirates for inter-system logistics.
This model has a small fixed missile point to the front.

A quick destroyer with a front-facing shield and some strong forward weaponry.
Dreamt up by ship-building prodigy, Graj Krell, as she sat in the bridge of her Boxer following a hard-fought battle, watching a Valkyrie loaded with precious goods limp away from her near-immobile fleet.
A brief meeting with the catering staff and a couple of afternoons later, she had come up with the basis of the Langoustine, a genuine attack destroyer.

A modestly armed, quick freighter, often used for intra-system cargo runs near to the Breh'Inni system.
The front-concentrated ballistic and missile mounts can allow for an effective combat vessel as part of a fleet, but a lightweight frame can make it vulnerable if caught alone.

A hardy and versatile explorer, designed for those times when the Junk Pirates need to go a bit further from home.
Not designed primarily as a combat vessel, however thick armour and the capability to mount a large energy weapon has meant that the Goat has been used in battle often enough.

The Junk Pirates' battleship, created only for warfare. With a fearsome ballistic broadside and versatile energy emplacements, this is not to be trifled with.
Heavy armour and a good shield allows it great staying power while the armaments deliver the pain.

The Turbot represents the apex of Junk Pirate technological lunacy, spearheaded by the notoriously paranoid philosopher-engineer, 'Angry' Jake Maddra. Originally laid down as a nimble strike craft, its entire internal volume has been violently hollowed out to accommodate the 'Heavy Interdiction Suite'. The sheer mass of jury-rigged capacitors and Domain-era electronic warfare projectors leaves the vessel sluggish and cumbersome to turn, but grants it an immense flux capacity and violent straight-line acceleration.
Because the Suite occupies almost all weapon hardpoints and ordnance space, the Turbot relies heavily on a specialized wing of autonomous Phase Drones. In combat, the Turbot acts as a sponge, intentionally soaking up energy before violently shunting its own accumulated flux directly into an enemy target, simultaneously driving its drone escorts into an electromagnetic feeding frenzy. Only 'Angry' Jake truly understands how the phase telemetry synchronizes with the interdictor pulse, but his paranoia ensures the blueprints will never see the light of day.
Quick, durable, and heavy hitting. This represents the best effort yet the Junk Pirates have made in achieving an effective fighter technology.

A massive, lumbering Frankenstein monster of a capital ship. The Reaper is a highly asymmetrical amalgamation of at least three distinct salvaged hulls—a boxy beige freighter block, heavy grey industrial gantries, and bizarre reddish-pink curved plating—all crudely welded together. Despite its chaotic, junk-heap appearance, it boasts tremendous raw bulk, reinforced by an always-on low-intensity structural integrity field that passively dampens incoming kinetic and energy trauma while housing the Junk Pirates' devastating accelerated particle drill.

Ostensibly a platform for experimental twinned PICA energy blasters. With a couple of makeshift engines attached, and the added punch of a large missile mount – the Magpie carries a dangerous assault package.
As far as it can be stated as such (given the inference of foresight not necessarily present in the original creation processes) the vessel is designed to burst in to the fray of lighter craft and demolish smaller hulls with the quick-moving and accurate bursts of fire from the two main weapons, supplemented by an all-round array of protective small energy weapons.
Energy transformation processes and flux handling is dealt with by a web of post-crystalline hyper-chained phase-polymers intertwined amongst the hulls, bulkheads and armour plating to give excellent performance in terms of capacities and dissipation.
The frontal shield protecting the relatively fragile armour gives survivability ratings above benchmarks for operational experimental space-laboratories in combat environments.

The final insult to many a marauding frigate hoping to find the gaps in the defenses of the lumbering hulk of The Kraken. Phase-beam wielding, displacer-capable and seemingly endless flux-handling capabilities - limited only by the tech that leashes the systems close to the Parent.

The Turbot carries a wing of high-tech drones capable of independently entering and exiting P-space. Armed with miniature pulse ion cannons, these agile drones flank enemy vessels to disable weapons, disrupt engines, and suppress hostile shielding.

The on-board workshops and manufacturing facilities located within the sweaty depths of The Reaper mining vessel are used for any number of things.
High stakes poker games and Chilli competitions entertain the crowds, the crushing and packing of ore feeds the growth of the Kingdom, and the constant replenishment of assault gun wielding drones allows the mothership to effectively break apart asteroids at dangerously close ranges, without worrying too much about asset losses.
The TNT drones provide a reasonable threat to attacking craft should The Reaper find itself without further support.

The partner drone to the assault gun wielding TNT drone. A point defense laser is used to interrogate cracks and fissures in the faces of ore-rich asteroids, where its bigger sister will follow with some explosive ordnance.
Provides useful point defense support in a combat situation.

A razor-sharp automated interceptor drone spawned by the Spinerette megastructure. Armed with an ion cannon and twin light machine guns, it aggressively swarms hostile strike craft and scrambles incoming missile salvos before they can threaten the hub.

A heavy automated combat drone deployed by the Spinerette automata cloud. Equipped with paired light mortars and an integrated flare defense system, it maintains persistent pressure against enemy hull plating in orbital defense engagements.

This is a huge, slithering mass of incoherent and unidentifiable modules, vaguely arranged in an Arachnoid manner. Strong energy signatures emanate from the central pod arrangement and a full-spectrum scan of this … thing … reveals no organic life.

Originally conceived as a joint venture between corporate interests and high-tech arms dealers, the Raven was intended to be a next-generation raider. The project collapsed amid infighting, leaving the Junk Pirates to salvage the surviving prototypes. While boasting advanced systems and an integrated targeting core, its rushed structural integration makes it a dangerous anomaly.

A lightweight mobile frigate outfitted with a small drone bay, carrying an ion-drone.
Limited offensive capabilities, but an excellent harasser in support of heavier ships.

The Wirefox is capable of meeting foes head-on, biting with some dangerous front-facing weaponry, and not letting go.
Needs support when outgunned due to its typical P.A.C.K. flimsy hull, but mobile enough to choose her battles.

The modified Shuttle-variant of the Wirefox-class frigate, often referred to as 'Smooth-Haired' due to the SH suffix printed on the hull - and an ironic dig at the down-on-their-luck pilots who - sooner or later - are destined to lose their hair.
Cheap to operate and field, and highly manoeuvrable - but lacking in genuine defensive capabilities.

Fierce, hardy and unrepentant. The Pitbull has been designed around the overclocked and brutal front-facing Ripsaw, a kinetic bombardment weapon based on the light autocannon.
All-round light ballistic protection and four wing-mounted missile mounts complete the payload of this dangerous and heavily armoured light destroyer.

The lifeblood of the P.A.C.K. fleet, the Ridgeback is capable of many roles, and an expert in none. Flexible weapon mountings allow this craft to perform adequately in a combat environment, although in catering for so many diverse supporting roles, with large cargo bays and complicated life-support systems, the hull is extraordinarily fragile for a ship of its size. Modern refits incorporate the Ridgeback Protocol, combining accelerated weapon autoloaders with dorsal thermal shunts to grant bursts of fierce firepower and agility when cornered.

A variant of the Ridgeback, the Ridgeback X is smaller, and being designed for operation in more extreme environments - with better flux management and heavier armour - is generally more suitable for a direct combat role. Fitted with the specialized Ridgeback Protocol, it combines robust armor protection with rapid-cycling ballistic firepower.

The Black Russian Terrier, more commonly known as the BRT seems to be designed around primarily an escort or point defense role.
The versatile mounts and reasonable flux management allow it to prosper in other more offensive roles. The large bridge structure allows for a relatively high personnel capacity.

This Black Russian Terrier (BRT) is a heavily modified version with an operating flight deck substituted in place of the normally forward-facing smaller weaponry of her cousin.
Canebianco technicians have baked-in advanced optics to supplement the retained Affenpinscher and any other beam weaponry the commander may wish to outfit within the two medium modular energy mounts.
Still kitted out with versatile mounts and reasonable flux management - it can be outfitted with a defensive or offensive standpoint. The large bridge structure allows for a relatively high personnel capacity.

A utility ship with a keen sensor system and a reasonable capacity for cargo, provides a good complement to a P.A.C.K. fleet.
Limited combat capabilities and a poor choice for offensive operations, but reasonable in a defensive role with her burn drive and dual medium ballistic turrets.
The Ion Drone of the Bedlington allows the ship to act as a very effective harasser
P.A.C.K. support drone implemented variously through the fleet to supplement the combat capabilities of the parent vessel.

Vulcans and Swarmers make the Ivan-class great for screening against opposition fighter wings.
The LPC has proc-gen code built in which provides a martially-useless but unique external decal-covering and finishing package to each unit - with common themes including neon under-carriage lighting; chromed front grilles and flame-effect fractal decals. These will often be supplemented by the Pilots own handiwork - although the mission-count of any individual unit will rarely hit double figures.

With a miniaturised Ripsaw mounted on each wing; The Alyosha-class is capable of punching above its weight and putting pressure on shielded vessels. Flares allow the gunships to provide additional interference.
The reliance on kinetic weaponry make the unit a specialised one; but when deployed correctly it can shift the tides of a close battle.

The Mitya-class has a couple of turret-mounted mag-rail delivered HE torpedoes; plus a shield and a PD laser to make sure it has a good chance of getting close enough to deliver.
The central command globe of this powerful bomber is particularly arcane in its construction and this unit is difficult for an autofac to efficiently field.

The Levin-class gunship is characterised by a huge frame for an LPC deliverable battle-platform - with a corresponding level of resilience under fire and lack of mobility.
Designed to deliver a heavy burst of fire from range with her onboard Thumper and LAG turrets; it suffers under prolonged individual engagements due to the heavy flux load of the very large ordnance it carries.
Onboard IPDAI assists in clearing away incoming missile threats but can distract from the primary role of the unit.

The Oblonsky-class is an entirely self-sufficient Carrier-driven, CPU-operated, vulcan-armed drone with one drawback - the units are pre-programmed to require pilots to even clear the deck-mounted autofac.
Once manned, the Oblonsky-class is capable of very-high mobility. A foam-metal-matrix filler subsumes the space between the pilot and the cockpit shell to protect from excessive forces at high speed; and a neural-spike allows the pilot to interface with the navigational and targeting computer - but the extremely high speeds of a typical space battle means the pilot rarely provides much in the way of meaningful input - the benefit being mostly to the pilot - with a brain quickly flooded with adrenaline, dopamine and any-other-mine the pituitary can squeeze out whilst the tiny craft corkscrews through open space.
Oblonsky pilots are variously revered and ridiculed as the age-old and culturally-independent debate on the issue of 'Bravery vs. Foolishness' merrily goes on throughout the many booze-halls and cat-houses of P.A.C.K. space.

A P.A.C.K. Cruiser with one notable strength - it is capable of maintaining 3 fighter wings on the battlefield.
Otherwise would only ever be described as 'adequate' - but with a moderately efficient shield and a reasonable logistical footprint, it provides a useful means for the P.A.C.K. fleet to bring any one of a number of Gunships to the field.
The craft is complete with an integrated, complex comms and control array capable of instigating 'Trilateral Augmentation Algorithms' via her gunships or fighters - using quantum computing to create a short term possibilities-forecast through interlinking carrier & fighter intel to greatly improve the fighters navigational processors over a brief period.

The Griffon Fauve de Bretagne - or more often referred to as GFB - is a destroyer-level combat carrier with an in-built Ivan Gunship wing, plus capability to mount one more of any other sector-wide modular fighter or gunship LPC.
Relatively heavily armoured, and highly mobile - this is a real front-line carrier with potentially devastating combat potential.

The Bully Kutta is a cumbersome but effective missile cruiser, which was originally designed to operate as an atmospheric landing vessel in politically and naturally hostile environments.
Due to the generous complement of missiles and unusually thick armour plating (allowing it to enter atmospheres and also to remain intact against the self-generated engine thrusts necessary to do so safely) this finds great use as a real heavy hitter – but due to the low mobility can find it difficult to engage threats without coordinated fleet manoeuvres generating sufficient interference elsewhere.

This is a frightening side-grade to the P.A.C.K. missile cruiser (the Bully Kutta), put in to use by pirate groups with a marked change of focus – the Dog Box concentrates more on the provision of ballistic weaponry and ditches most safety protocols.
The Bully Kutta itself is a cumbersome cruiser, which was originally designed to operate as an atmospheric landing vessel in politically and naturally hostile environments. The Dog Box is an attempt to move the Bully Kutta frame in to a proper assault role – using the heavy armour alongside safety overrides to theoretically combine in allowing it to engage at short range – where the lumbering Bully Kutta could not.
A light freighter, capable of running loads at decent speeds and good fuel economy. Reasonably well armed but with poor manoeuvrability, is of limited value in combat scenarios.
The Samoyed freighter has been detached from the primary cargo vessel, increasing combat viability markedly.

The Komondor guard destroyer appears to be of a higher technological level than the bulk of the P.A.C.K. fleet, and carries a very versatile set of generally forward facing weapon mounts. Blessed with a thick suit of armour, lower crew levels and an uncharacteristically thick hull, it has decent staying power at the cost of some agility in combat. An experimental Tri-Feed Overcharge synchronizes its formidable weapon battery, allowing it to function as a devastating frontline brawler.

Large and well-armoured with a wide omni-directional shield and an oversized, rudimentary phase coil that enables the ship to take small stutters across wrinkles of p-space.
The Shar Pei represents a snapshot in P.A.C.K. technology at a time pre-expansion when phase space was being experimented with, rather than mastered - by the engineers of the time.
A cautious captain uses the craft from range, with missile and ballistic support and avoiding fire with the P.A.C.K. phase skimmer. An aggressive captain hops in to close range through p-space and uses an impressive outfit of weaponry to quickly disable the target before the comparatively thick layer of armour can be breached.

This Shar-Pei class vessel has been modified heavily by Canebianco technicians to amplify the power core output by a couple of orders of magnitude. The impact, as was theorised, is that the skimmer system will now hold the ship stable in p-space.
With the strategic boon of being a capable phase ship, it is broadly similar to the Shar-Pei. The modifications do however include a necessary increase to the flux capacity, swapping out the front mounted missile hardpoints for energy, and some bright spark added a handy energy-bypass to allow the ship to operate as if it has a High Energy Focus system.

An unusually large P.A.C.K. spacefaring vessel with good speed and agility and potential to deliver massive damage with a big bite from the forward facing missile and energy weaponry. Once she has got a grip, she can be difficult to shake off in a one-on-one battle due to her manoeuvring jets.

Big, ugly, and powerful - but a history of introspective and destructive design iteration means it is no longer the ultimate fighting dog that it once was.
The original designs were, at one point, best in class and this vessel was a key tactical piece in the Kollective achieving the segregation that they so desired. As the Bulldog saw fewer and fewer engagements, and the relevant technical minds rotted through generations of isolation, without enough self-awareness or foresight, the systems were (at best) never suitably upgraded (or at worst) inadvertently down-specified against a comparable machine in another part of the sector.
Whilst it does not compare favourably in terms of ordnance load or flux handling to the other key players in its weight-class - two front facing closely focused large ballistic mounts and exceptional all round coverage make it a very dangerous foe in shorter evenly-matched engagements against most ships.
text3: Cementing its status as a resilient fleet anchor, the modern Bulldog is equipped with the 'Alpha Call' wolfpack coordination array. This advanced tactical suite allows it to seamlessly direct allied strikes and command the vanguard of any P.A.C.K. formation.

The original designs were, at one point, best in class and this vessel was a key tactical piece in the Kollective achieving the segregation that they so desired. As the Bulldog saw fewer and fewer engagements, and the relevant technical minds rotted through generations of isolation, without enough self-awareness or foresight, the systems were (at best) never suitably upgraded (or at worst) inadvertently down-specified against a comparable machine in another part of the sector. This particular version has had a lot of these design errors corrected, and is significantly more dangerous than the base-spec Bulldog.
This particular Bulldog does compare favourably to the other key players in its weight-class - and with three front facing closely focused large ballistic mounts, an ammo-feed system and exceptional all round coverage - don't get caught in front of this monster.

An agile frigate with an unusual capacity for handling flux dissipation, unfortunately the agility and dissipation are possible largely by foregoing protective armour measures.
Excels as a point defense escort craft due to four light energy turrets providing coverage in all directions, coupled with the exceptional flux dissipation rate. A brave captain can utilise the Schnauzer in many roles, including strike and assault, but the lightweight frame and poor dissipation with the shield up makes it unsuitable generally for direct engagements with larger craft.

An orbital station bearing the markings of Pre-P.A.C.K. Anarchist Groups. This platform hosts shipyards, habitats, factories, and large stockpiles of weapons and supplies allowing projection of military and industrial power throughout the local orbital volume.

An orbital station bearing the markings of Pre-P.A.C.K. Anarchist Groups. This platform hosts shipyards, habitats, factories, and large stockpiles of weapons and supplies allowing projection of military and industrial power throughout the local orbital volume.
A rarely seen adaptation of the ubiquitous ASP freighter / carrier. This version is significantly better armed including the in-built pair of ‘Typewriter’ point defense machine guns.

Cruiser-sized freighter, built around the speedy delivery of cargo.
Flight deck and hangar space allows for a versatile fighter escort, but low ordnance capability (especially compared to the hull size) means the on-board armaments can be limited.

Large and relatively fast cargo craft, with a reasonable combat capability.
Still needs heavy support when operating outside the more civilized sectors, but a shrewd captain can move a lot of cargo, and get very rich, very fast. The on-board flight deck means that these are quite often escorted by a significant fighter force, which are additionally supplemented by the ships ‘Targeting Feed’ system.

A frighteningly militarized overhaul of the standard ASP heavy freighter, customized in secret drydocks by the Syndicate's ruthless Familia enforcers. Stripping away civilian cargo bays and automated freight gantries, the Gigantophis (F) is reconstructed entirely around a spinal-mounted ASP Viper Pulse Cannon—a jury-rigged heavy plasma projector capable of firing rapid, punishing bursts of high-velocity violet bolts that overwhelm hostile shields and fracture armor plating. Supported by auxiliary maneuvering thrusters and dedicated strike fighter bays, this sinister warship transforms a docile bulk transport into a devastating assault carrier.

Quick and lightly armed courier craft.
Good speed and fair manoeuvrability still make it a capable combat craft, but low ordnance potential means the captain needs to be selective in the choice of weaponry.
A modified version of the common Diamondback – this is significantly less common and a lot more dangerous.

This is a run of the mill combat freighter – with no particular outstanding strengths or weaknesses – and a single refittable flight deck.
Holds its own in medium-sized fleets when a smaller dedicated freighter just doesn’t have enough teeth.
An upgunned (and rare) version of the base Hognose; a medium sized ballistic hardpoint allows this light destroyer to become a serious threat on the battlefield.

A capital-grade vessel built explicitly for the purposes of exploration. Capable of operating for a reasonable length of time with minimal logistic support, and offering class-leading fuel economy.
The internals of the craft are punctuated with multiple snaking corridors bridging large open fab-decks with smaller sub-voids providing container space, sleeping accommodation and control suites. The fab-decks provide in-flight synthesis of various goods (allowing for a reduced supply footprint) as well as feeding the 4 bays up front of the craft. These 4 bays allow for the deployment of (variously) probes, surface drones and half-tracks, sens-nets and up to 3 refittable LPC fighter craft.
An in-built ‘Death Rattle’ support wing alongside some modest weaponry round out the offensive capability of the craft – which in line with the rest of the ASP Doctrine tends towards providing a deterrent rather than a true capital-grade offensive capability.

A modified, and rarely seen, version of the ASP fleet’s explorer, the King Cobra. Where the parent ship concentrates on fuel economy and survey capabilities; this particular craft concentrates on the provision of terrible firepower in the form of 3 large missile mounts.
Heavy support fighter with an extremely useful flak cannon. Limited offensive capability but provides exceptional defensive support for the parent carrier.

A large and powerful fighter craft widely used in escorting ASP fleets outside of the safer courier routes.
A major deterrent for frigates and opposition fighters, and difficult to take down for everybody. Much like the other ASP fighter craft, will struggle to bring a true offensive capability to the battlefield outside of small-scale skirmishes - but by the time this thing has done its job causing interference throughout the battlefield - the mission payload can often be ready to engage a sustained burn in hyperspace.

Capable and versatile fighter craft, designed to combat other fighter and bomber threats.
Sporting a couple of mining lasers and a pack of swarmers, the Venom struggles against anything of real size.

Lightweight drone that carries a low support profile, and is cheap.
Often deployed to escort the ASP syndicate fleet in civilized space, where a deterrent is more important than a genuine combat threat.

An early precursor to Phase technology, the P.A.C.K. phase skimmer achieves an effect very similar to that seen on the Wolf-class and the Medusa-class craft.
This prototypical system is large, cumbersome, flux-hungry but generally very stable. This P.A.C.K. technology utilises a large phase coil to bring the body of the ship in to p-space via the singular discharge of a liquid copper 1.2 teraCoulomb capacitor. This metamotion causes a huge inductive load to spike back through the coil, which in turn fires through a secondary super-cooled electromagnet, pulling space in to small local wrinkles and snapping the craft back to n-space, at a slightly different location.
text3: An early precursor to Phase technology, the P.A.C.K. phase skimmer achieves an effect very similar to that seen on the Wolf-class and the Medusa-class craft.

text1: Crew divert power and cooling from major auxiliary systems directly to the engine thrusters, granting a significant temporary surge in speed and maneuverability.
text3: Temporarily increases top speed and maneuverability at the cost of shield and weapons efficiency.

text1:
The engine is temporarily increased in thrust and controls locked. Allows limited increase in battlefield mobility, as long as you want to go in a straight line.
Borrowing a lot of technology from the commonly applied Expansion-tech 'Burn Drive', this particular system is ostensibly a reverse engineered; modified version of the same which allows the shield to remain active whilst limiting total active power. On activation the crew are - every time - met by the holo-signature of revered Canebianco technician 'Tricot Raye' dramatically explaining the relevant safety-protocols. Such was the techincal skill (and ego) of Raye in the implementation, ongoing P.A.C.K.-wide efforts to unlock and circumvent this repetitive, overdone and badly delivered soliloquy are failing.
text3: The engine is temporarily increased in thrust and controls locked. Allows limited increase in battlefield mobility, as long as you want to go in a straight line.

text1: The crew divert their attention from engine related issues towards the shield, allowing the shield flux management systems to operate more efficiently.
text3: Diverts power to shield projectors to increase shield efficiency and dissipation.

text1:
A trilateral comms link is engaged between the carrier and each wing using an on-board single-threaded quantum CPU. The automated feedback-loops alternate between three craft at a time; creating a 'possibilities-forecast' matrix - predicting optimal courses of navigation and collision avoidance for all forseeable courses of action over a brief period.
This enhanced intel-map allows each fighter to push their speed and manoeuvrability envelope well over the norm whilst still maintaining collision events within tolerance.
text3: This enhanced intel-map allows each fighter to push their speed and manoeuvrability envelope well over the norm whilst still maintaining collision events within tolerance.

text1: Pre-charged cylinders of various cryo-gases are discharged into the various engine mechanisms aboard the ship – allowing the engines to run hot, boosting ship mobility temporarily. The discarded cylinders or ‘plugs’ carry a significant electrostatic charge and have been known to provide a suitable level of interference against minor missile threats on the battlefield.
text3: Increases mobility and provides for flare-like discharge of cryo-liquid ‘plugs’.

text1:
The Mass Ejection Retreat MechANism or MERMAN allows the hulking, lumbering, virtually immobile bulk of an overcommitted and inevitably overfluxed Kraken to go backwards relatively quickly.
There is no specific recipe for what gets chucked out of the front, but it is widely believed that using plugged-in CRT display screens (coupled to small but appropriately sized lead-acid UPS battery systems) brings good luck on the battlefield. It also allows for the fairly easy disposal of obsolete technology.
text3: The ship is forced backwards by the forward discharge of large quantities of mass. Locks out controls and drops shield.

text1: Launches chaff particles carrying a heavy electrostatic charge to interfere with the targeting systems of hostile PD weapons and incoming missiles. After a short charging period, chaff will release an EMP arc targeting a nearby hostile missile within a small radius.
text3: Launches electrostatically charged chaff particles to defend against nearby enemy missiles.

text1:
Dumping cryo-liquids from half-tonne Vacuum Insulated Evaporator tanks straight in to and around the cooling jackets of the ships engines allows for large ships to perform minor miracles in manoeuvrability – at least for a short while. The used vessels when ejected break up to form electrostatically charged debris which functionally act as flares.
In theory this will massively shorten the economic life of the particular vessels engine train and in order to mollify the engineering teams is often applied with a simple modification to allow for the efficient production and packaging of frozen dairy products.
text3: Increases mobility and provides for flare-like discharge of cryo-liquid ‘plugs’.

text1: Temporarily overcharges the localized structural fields, significantly increasing damage resistance.
text3: Overcharges structural fields to dramatically reduce damage taken.

text1: Deploys an autonomous wing of heavy industrial welding and excavation drones to assist the mothership in point-defense and close-range tactical fire.
text3: Deploys autonomous mining and point-defense drones.

text1: Charges a high-voltage electrostatic discharge array that arcs into nearby hostile ordnance and enemy fighter hulls, scrambling electronic systems and detonating missile warheads prematurely.
text3: Discharges high-voltage EMP arcs targeting nearby enemy missiles and craft.

text1: Originally salvaged from repurposed Domain-era electronic warfare arrays, the Heavy Interdiction Suite is a massive, jury-rigged amalgamation of high-yield capacitors and raw EM projectors. When triggered, it discharges a blinding interdiction pulse that overwhelms a single target's systems from afar. The sheer electromagnetic force forces a complete engine flameout, temporarily locks out the target's active ship systems and point-defense grids, and heavily suppresses their navigational agility. More terrifyingly, the array acts as a weaponized heat-sink: it violently siphons 40% of the host ship's accumulated flux and shunts it directly into the target, forcing catastrophic system overloads on the enemy while simultaneously flooding allied Phase Drones with an overcharged signal that drives them into an aggressive assault frenzy. Firing the array is incredibly taxing on the host hull, permanently degrading its combat readiness with each use.
text3: Shuts engines off, disables PD, locks ship systems, cuts agility, and shunts flux.

text1: Massive multi-tonne Vacuum Insulated Evaporator tanks dump high-density cryo-liquids directly into the supermassive sub-light thrusters of capital vessels, providing an instantaneous +40 boost to forward speed. The discarded heavy canisters eject as electrostatically charged chaff that decimate incoming missile arrays.
text3: Provides an instant forward boost to speed and launches charged chaff.

text1: The flagship broadcasts an encrypted tactical telemetry burst, designating an enemy target as the quarry and rallying nearby allied craft. The flagship gains improved flux dissipation and weapon handling, while nearby escorts receive speed and fire rate coordination. The targeted vessel suffers localized electronic warfare jamming, degrading its weapon tracking.
text3: Designates an enemy quarry, coordinating allied escorts and jamming the target.
text5: Increases flagship and allied escort speed, maneuverability, and rate of fire while disrupting the quarry's weapon aim.

text1: Temporarily bypasses weapon feed safeties across all mounts, accelerating the ship's ballistic autoloaders, energy capacitor cycling, and missile rack loaders. The synchronized feed system significantly boosts rate of fire while moderating weapon flux generation.
text3: Increases rate of fire across all weapons and reduces energy and ballistic flux generation.
text5: Increases ballistic, energy, and missile rate of fire by {{15%}}, and reduces ballistic and energy weapon flux generation by {{15%}}.

text1: Activates dorsal thermal shunt heat pipes along the ship's armored spine while engaging high-cycle weapon feeds. The rapid heat dissipation and accelerated firing cycle allow the ship to sustain aggressive gun runs and nimble maneuvering without risking reactor overload.
text3: Increases flux dissipation, rate of fire, and maneuverability while reducing weapon flux generation.
text5: Increases flux dissipation by {{40%}}, reduces weapon flux generation by {{25%}}, and increases weapon rate of fire by {{15%}}. Also provides a moderate boost to speed and maneuverability.

text1: A targeted refractive shield matrix projected onto a hostile vessel up to 900 su away, forcing a rapidly collapsing 360-degree shield containment prison around their hull. The overwhelming pressure of the collapsing bubble deals energy damage to armor and hull while weapon feeds are suppressed and internal flux rises rapidly. External weapon fire is absorbed by the matrix shell. Attempting to encompass a capital-class vessel requires exponentially more energy to maintain the matrix; a feat considered too taxing and frankly wasteful by Junk Pirate engineers.
text3: Traps a cruiser-sized or smaller enemy in a 3.5s shield prison, isolating them, crushing their hull, and building flux.

text1: A searing, rocky-metallic husk world perpetually roasted by the fierce crimson glare of Breh'Inni. The planet's fractured crust is cleaved by an endless network of jagged tectonic canyons, littered to unknown depths with rejected industrial slag, scorched starship frames, and abandoned mining infrastructure. Within subterranean fissures and pressurized dome clusters, an eccentric, self-governing commune of outlaw tinkerers, scrapper artists, and black-market electronics hackers thrives beyond the formal reach of Glory's King.

A turbulent gas giant enveloped in swirling bands of copper, rust, and dull amber. While extreme gravitational compression and scalding core temperatures prevent Backspin from igniting as a brown dwarf, its upper troposphere is infamous across the Breh'Inni system as the premier proving ground for Junk Pirate fighter pilots. The high orbital corridor is choked with a perpetual ring of perforated, drifting hulls—mute testaments to generations of live-fire dogfighting exercises and botched high-gravity maneuvers.

A freezing, cryogenic world of ammonia and methane glaciers where water-ice behaves with the hardness of granite, forming jagged mountain ranges and vast frozen plains. Sprawling across the sub-surface and winding through the lower atmosphere is a monumental, Domain-era network of crystalline metallo-ceramic hab-tubes. Now occupied by the eccentric nobility and scrapper syndicates of the Junk Pirates, Glory serves as the bustling capital of the Kingdom—a chaotic hub of jury-rigged shipyards, lawless bazaars, and industrial foundries.

A majestic, indigo-veiled gas giant whose immense hydrogen-rich atmosphere is crowned by a striking system of shimmering icy dust rings. Deep within its crushing mantle, astronomical pressures compress hydrogen into an exotic metallic slurry. Hope stands as a vital navigational beacon on the outer approach to Glory, its expansive ring planes frequently used by scrapper fleets and raiders to mask their thermal signatures before jumping through the system gate.

A desolate outer world of methane ice and razor-sharp silicate ridges. Due to the eccentric orbit and faint warmth of the distant primary, a tenuous volatile atmosphere sublimates along the day side, only to precipitate violently as caustic crystalline snow when rotating into the freezing night. The surface is heavily scarred by automated scoops and low-altitude harvesters dispatched by the neighboring N.O.M.D.E. station.

A desolate rocky-metallic planet on the frozen fringe of the Breh'Inni system. Over centuries, Too Far has served as an unintentional firing range and dumping ground for errant mass-driver payloads ejected by N.O.M.D.E., as well as countless jettisoned radioactive reactor cores from passing scrapper fleets. Its rugged highlands cast an eerie, phosphorescent gleam in the void from the sheer concentration of pulverized synthetic matter and irradiated debris.

A scorched, metallic world orbiting in close proximity to the red dwarf Canis. Stripped of any meaningful atmosphere by millennia of stellar flares, Spot is surrounded by a dense ring of pulverized ore and asteroidal debris known as Spot's Belt. Its mineral-rich crust and the sheltered radar shadows within the surrounding ring system make it a favored staging ground for outlaw raiders and corsairs.

A frigid, crater-pocked world of silicate rock and dirty water-ice. Hooch exists in perpetual twilight, its barren surface shadowed by drifting orbital wreckage and old battle debris. Rumors persist among local smugglers that forgotten fuel caches and illicit cargo drops are hidden within its deep glacial rifts.

A colossal gas giant enveloped in an eerie, luminous emerald shroud. Beneath Petra's upper cloud decks lie the floating atmospheric arcologies and industrial habitats of the Post-Anarchist Canis Kollective. Generations of heavy atmospheric processing and closed-loop synthetic recycling have saturated the surrounding troposphere with radioactive heavy metals and toxic isotopes, turning the planet's protective veil into a suffocating environmental crisis that now forces the Kollective out into the Sector.

A restless, cryovolcanic outer world whose methane-frosted surface is regularly reshaped by towering geysers of supercooled ammonia and slurry. Orbiting on the outer rim of Canis near the primary jump-point, Laika serves as an icy watchpost and navigational reference for inbound fleets.

A desolate, cinder-baked world nearest to the bright yellow star Ursulo. Rupert's surface is heavily pitted with impact craters and the glassed scars of kinetic strikes dating back to early corporate border disputes, leaving behind a sterile wasteland of irradiated basalt.

A dense, rocky-metallic planet rich in heavy ores and rare elements. Winnipeg bears the unmistakable gouges and strip-mining trenches left by aggressive corporate extraction projects during the expansion era, now standing as a desolate metallic monument to unbridled industrial exploitation.

An arid, sun-bleached world dominated by vast expanses of shifting dunes and jagged mountain ranges. Violent seasonal dust fronts ravage the equatorial wastes, forcing the bulk of the population into fortified mega-cities and high-density corporate arcologies clustered along the temperate tropics. Under the sleek veneer of legitimate interstellar shipping, Paddington is the seat of the ASP Syndicate—a thriving nexus of underworld finance, high-volume logistics, and aggressive corporate syndicates.

A massive, violet-and-indigo banded gas giant holding sway over the outer reaches of the Ursulo system. Aloysius anchors vast Trojan asteroid clusters at its Lagrange points, creating a haven of navigational dead-zones favored by smugglers and rogue fleets seeking to evade Syndicate patrol sweeps.

From orbit, Yogi presents the stunning image of a lush, pristine terran paradise with azure seas and rolling green continents. In reality, vast swathes of the emerald 'forests' are meticulously painted roofs covering sprawling, high-capacity petrochemical and antimatter fuel refineries. Through remarkably advanced filtration grids, the planetary ecosystem is kept just stable enough to sustain a comfortable standard of living for corporate executives and industrial laborers alike.

The pale, cryovolcanic moon of Paddington. Baloo's surface is mapped with glittering fields of frozen nitrogen and active cryo-geysers that vent shimmering plumes into the void. Its stark, frozen horizon provides a dramatic backdrop to the endless stream of commercial traffic arriving at Paddington's orbital approaches.

A searing rocky-metallic world closest to the star York. Rich veins of heavy metals pit its cratered crust, though intense solar radiation makes surface operations hazardous without orbital shielding.
A small frozen world composed of rock and water ice. The planetary surface is crisscrossed by deep cryogenic glaciers and sparse automated surveying outposts.
The wholesomeness of Lincoln can almost be seen from space. The planet is often used by the Hegemony to demonstrate the success of their policies in bringing order and stability back to the sector.

A massive, sickly-yellow gas giant slowly tracing the outer frontier of the system. Swanage is characterized by violent equatorial wind shears, dense radiation belts, and a prominent retinue of captured moons. While its upper atmosphere is rich in harvestable isotopes, commercial exploitation is heavily hampered by the presence of rogue raider cells and anomalous Pre-Collapse structures anchored in its orbital plane.

The frozen wastes of Dartmouth are bound in eternal frost, its rugged highlands crisscrossed by an extensive network of Domain-era metallo-ceramic hab-tubes. Unlike the bustling conduits on Glory, the structures here have fallen into cold silence—their life support systems long drained, their sealed bulkheads preserving forgotten Pre-Collapse survey archives and frozen machinery that draw intrepid salvage expeditions.

Orbiting directly opposite its dormant sister Dartmouth, Christchurch possesses a substantially intact and functional network of Domain hab-tubes. Pressurized by geothermal tap-wells and heavy life-support matrices, these tubular subterranean arcologies provide a vital, heavily fortified frontier outpost for the PACK Kollective, enabling deep-range patrol coordination and local mineral processing.

It is not clear how the orbital station at Lincoln originally became known as 'the Cathedral' - however Hegemony propaganda places it highly as a point of pilgrimage for space travellers. Particularly those in the import / export business.

A sprawling orbital scrap-citadel and the supreme military command center of the Junk Pirates, orbiting perilously low within Backspin's upper gravity well. The station's heavy armored superstructure shimmers with a menacing red hue under the light of Breh'Inni, scarred by near-constant impacts from hypervelocity debris. Within its labyrinthine hangar bays and live-fire simulation corridors, the King's most ruthless fighter aces and fleet commanders are hardened through relentless attrition.

The crowning jewel of the ASP Syndicate's commercial empire, Paddington Station is a colossal, multi-tiered orbital transit hub. Thousands of armored freighters, express couriers, and discreet corporate shuttles dock daily at its automated berths, where billions of credits in licit and illicit goods change hands in luxurious executive suites and shadowy under-deck concourses.

A sleek, gleaming Tri-Tachyon orbital installation whose pristine corporate geometry stands in stark contrast to the roughshod settlements of the Canis system. Ostensibly an advanced tech-mining logistics and salvage hub, the station serves as a secure listening post and research facility tasked with dissecting the Kollective's unorthodox phase-skimmer technology.

A fortified orbital base built into a hollowed-out nickel-iron asteroid above Spot. Jameson Orbital serves as the undisputed bastion of pirate warlords in the Canis system, featuring heavily reinforced docking bays, clandestine munitions depots, and raucous mercenary dens that project corsair power across the inner trade routes.

A colossal, segmented megastructure of unknown Domain or Pre-Collapse provenance, drifting in silent orbit around the gas giant. Resembling an immense metallic arachnid, the Spinerette is believed to have been an automated nano-assembly web-spinner responsible for extruding and laying the miles of metallo-ceramic hab-tubes found throughout the sector. Though currently inert, residual energy readings pulse deep within its central nexus.

A churning, luminous cloud of self-replicating nano-assemblers and autonomous construction automata swarming around an ancient spinal chassis. Crackling with coherent energy discharges, the cloud extends shimmering crystalline tendrils deep into the planetary atmosphere, actively harvesting matter and weaving complex megastructures in an eerie manifestation of unrestrained Pre-Collapse geo-engineering.

A geometric framework composed of an impossibly dense, non-reflective adamantine alloy, hovering silently in space. The artifact exhibits electromagnetic resonance patterns and spatial warping signatures remarkably akin to the inactive Domain Gate network, yet its precise function and origin remain an unsettling mystery to even the most experienced salvagers.

The skeletal, twisted carcass of an ancient capital-class industrial vessel or station module, slowly tumbling along a decaying orbital trajectory. Corrosive stellar winds and micrometeorite impacts continue to strip metallic fragments from its ribs, producing dazzling streaks of atmospheric entry fire as discarded bulkheads plunge toward the world below.

The Nearly There Orbital Mass Driver Experiment (N.O.M.D.E.) is a colossal, jury-rigged industrial extraction platform tethered above the frozen crust of Nearly There. Originally constructed to harvest volatile slurry for an eccentric, long-abandoned planetary siege cannon, the station has evolved into a bustling volatile mining hive. Massive magnetic coils still periodically test-fire high-velocity slug canisters across the outer system, to the constant annoyance and terror of nearby shipping.

A massive, heavily armored industrial station drifting through the volatile-rich Fireworks Belt. Serving as the primary weapons foundry and ordnance testing ground for the ASP Syndicate, the station echoes with the thunder of constant munitions fabrication. Behind blast-shielded bulkheads and black-market storefronts, the ruthless ASP Familia manufactures illicit explosives and enforces syndicate contracts.

An unruly, sprawling mining citadel anchored within the dense ice and ore bands of Finnigan's Gift. Operating largely outside any central authority, the station is a chaotic hive of independent prospectors, black-market ore smelters, and heavily armed gun-runners trading raw asteroid yield for refined fuel and weaponry.

Perpetually cast in deep shadow within the immense umbra of Aloysius, Bear's Pit is widely regarded as one of the most ruthless outlaw stations in the sector. Free from the formal oversight of the Syndicate, it operates as a lawless pirate haven where black-market cargo is fenced, bounties are brokered, and disputes are settled through swift violence.

An isolated deep-space research installation constructed during the early anarchist secession. The station contains networks of specialized laboratory bays, quantum computation nodes, and prototype sensor arrays originally designed to explore exotic phase phenomena and closed-loop biosystems. Closer inspection may yield valuable salvage.

An automated asteroid-mining platform bearing the faded insignias of early Pre-PACK anarchist collectives. Though officially decommissioned, its heavy ore processors and extraction gantries remain semi-intact, with faint power signatures suggesting salvageable machinery and forgotten mineral caches within its pressurized vaults.

A communal orbital habitat module dating to the initial migration of the Canis anarchist factions. Emergency auxiliary reactors continue to maintain rudimentary atmosphere in sealed compartments, where surviving data logs, personal effects, and forgotten supplies await discovery.

A vast network of Domain-era metallo-ceramic habitation tubes woven across the planetary surface and subsurface crust. These ancient atmospheric conduits provide sheltered living volumes and life-support stabilization, significantly lowering planetary hazard.

An extensive network of Domain-era habitation tubes intertwined with the crust and atmosphere. The ancient orbital automata cloud remains active, relentlessly expanding the construction with volatile nanite emissions and aggressive drone patrols that pose a severe hazard to colonists.

Headquarters of the ASP Familia, the syndicate's feared enforcement branch. Embedded deep within corporate structures, this organization coordinates privateer fleets and heavy enforcement operations to safeguard Syndicate trade dominance.

Even though the majority of financial transactions can be carried out remotely and reliably from just about any point in the sector, sometimes this hyper-connectedness can lead to a level of scrutiny that certain individuals do not always appreciate.
In that case, physically moving money by decrypted credit chips is an archaic (but widely accepted) way to ensure a certain level of opacity can be maintained, which works great assuming you can trust whoever is carrying your chips for you.

The Junk Pirates are a motley collection of individuals, cults and sub-factions based in the Breh'Inni system - living throughout the arcane domain-tech hab-tubes knitted through the mantle and lower atmosphere of the freezing world of Glory.
Whilst these groups are disparate and many-faceted as individuals, they are bound together by a cultural affinity and appreciation of technology.
The other almost universally shared attribute is a belief in a lack of formal establishment (beyond the pseudo-monarchic ranking on Breh'Inni under the King), and a subsequent dislike of the larger factions.

The Associated Starline Parcels Syndicate were once a simple corporate courier – grown large through financially and socially aggressive mergers, acquisitions and backroom deals
Their home planet (Paddington in the system of Ursulo) is haunted by a pervasive criminal underworld, but the services and commercial dealings of the syndicate leave them in a positive standing to most of the major factions.

The Post Anarchist Canis Kollective have recently emerged from under a thick and increasingly toxic atmosphere of Petra, a shield for centuries which kept them hidden from outsiders.
In recent times it has become a smothering blanket, as the technology which has kept them in food, supplies and energy by resynthesising the atmospheric material has rejected non-ideal isotopes and compounds back to the planet to the point where the existence of the colony is threatened.
In their emergence they are socially and technologically unprepared for the current state of the sector.

The Viper Pulse Cannon is a heavily modified underworld knockoff of the Hegemony's Thermal Pulse Cannon. Built directly into the prow of ASP Familia enforcer vessels, it overcharges its containment coils to violently expel a 5-round burst of high-velocity violet plasma, trading the raw thermal efficiency of the original for raw, destabilizing EMP damage.
